module LinkedQueue : QueueInterface.QUEUE = struct

  type 'a qnode = { v: 'a;
                    mutable next: 'a qnode option }

  type 'a queue = { mutable head: 'a qnode option;
                    mutable tail: 'a qnode option }

  (* INVARIANT:
   - q.head and q.tail are either both None, or
   - q.head and q.tail both point to Some nodes, and
       - q.tail is reachable by following 'next' pointers
         from q.head
       - q.tail's next pointer is None *)

    { head = None;
      tail = None }

  let enq (elt: 'a) (q: 'a queue) : unit =
    let newnode = Some { v = elt; next = None } in
    begin match q.tail with
    | None ->
       (* Note that the invariant tells us that q.head is also None *)
       q.head <- newnode;
       q.tail <- newnode
    | Some n ->
       n.next <- newnode;
       q.tail <- newnode
    end

     a queue with v1 at the head and vn at the tail. Do not use any
     List library functions. Your solution must be tail recursive. *)

  (* ----------------------------------------------------------------
     Everything from here to the end of the module is provided for testing.
     You don't need to read or change any of it.
     ---------------------------------------------------------------- *)

  let rec find_last_node (qn: 'a qnode) : 'a qnode option =
    let rec loop (curr: 'a qnode) (seen: 'a qnode list) : 'a qnode option =
      begin match curr.next with
      | None -> Some curr
      | Some n ->
        let rec contains_alias (qnl :'a qnode list) : 'a qnode option =
          begin match qnl with
          | [] -> loop n (curr :: seen)
          | h :: t -> if n == h then None else contains_alias t
          end in
        contains_alias seen
      end
    in loop qn []

  let valid (q: 'a queue) : bool =
    begin match q.head, q.tail with
    | None, None -> true
    | Some qh, Some qt ->
       begin match find_last_node qh with
       | Some n -> qt == n (* the tail points to the last node *)
       | None -> false
       end
    | _, _ -> false
    end

  let is_empty (q: 'a queue) : bool =
    q.head = None

  let deq (q: 'a queue) : 'a option =
    begin match q.head with
    | None ->
       None
    | Some n ->
       q.head <- n.next;
       begin match n.next with
       | None -> q.tail <- None; Some n.v
       | Some _ -> Some n.v
       end
    end

  let to_list (q: 'a queue) : 'a list =
    let rec loop (no: 'a qnode option) (l: 'a list) : 'a list =
      begin match no with
      | None -> List.rev l
      | Some n -> loop n.next (n.v :: l)

problems.extraTests:
(* Test helpers: build a deque by hand and check its links. *)
let deque_of_list (l : 'a list) : 'a deque =
  let d = { head = None; tail = None } in
  let rec go (l : 'a list) : unit =
    begin match l with
    | [] -> ()
    | x :: rest ->
      let n = { v = x; next = None; prev = d.tail } in
      begin match d.tail with
      | None -> d.head <- Some n
      | Some t -> t.next <- Some n
      end;
      d.tail <- Some n;
      go rest
    end
  in
  go l; d

(* Elements read from head to tail by following next pointers. *)
let forward_list (q : 'a deque) : 'a list =
  let rec loop (no : 'a dqnode option) (acc : 'a list) : 'a list =
    begin match no with
    | None -> List.rev acc
    | Some n -> loop n.next (n.v :: acc)
    end
  in
  loop q.head []

let ends_ok (q : 'a deque) : bool =
  begin match q.head, q.tail with
  | None, None -> true
  | Some h, Some t ->
    (match h.prev with None -> true | Some _ -> false)
    && (match t.next with None -> true | Some _ -> false)
  | _ -> false
  end

let consistent (q : 'a deque) : bool =
  ends_ok q && forward_list q = to_list q

let test () : bool =
  let d = create () in
  reverse d; to_list d = [] && consistent d
;; run_test "reverse: empty deque" test

module Assert = struct
(* Minimal stand-in for the CIS 1200 Assert module.
   run_test prints one line per test; a summary is printed at exit. *)

let passed = ref 0
let failed = ref 0

let report (desc : string) (ok : bool) (detail : string) : unit =
  if ok then (incr passed; Printf.printf "PASS  %s\n%!" desc)
  else (incr failed; Printf.printf "FAIL  %s%s\n%!" desc
          (if detail = "" then "" else "  (" ^ detail ^ ")"))

let run_test (desc : string) (f : unit -> bool) : unit =
  match f () with
  | true -> report desc true ""
  | false -> report desc false "returned false"
  | exception Stack_overflow -> report desc false "stack overflow: not tail recursive?"
  | exception e -> report desc false ("raised " ^ Printexc.to_string e)

(* Passes when f raises an exception. *)
let run_failing_test (desc : string) (f : unit -> bool) : unit =
  match f () with
  | _ -> report desc false "expected an exception"
  | exception _ -> report desc true ""

let test_property_on (name : string) (prop : 'a -> bool) (inputs : 'a list) : unit =
  List.iteri
    (fun i x -> run_test (Printf.sprintf "%s (input %d)" name (i + 1)) (fun () -> prop x))
    inputs

let summary () : unit =
  Printf.printf "SUMMARY %d/%d passed\n%!" !passed (!passed + !failed)

(* Size of the "large input" tests that check for tail recursion. *)
let stress_n = 1000


(* Tail-recursive List.init, so building big test inputs never uses the stack. *)
let tr_init (n : int) (f : int -> 'a) : 'a list =
  let rec go (i : int) (acc : 'a list) : 'a list =
    if i < 0 then acc else go (i - 1) (f i :: acc)
  in
  go (n - 1) []
end
